title: How to Close the Deal Visibility Gap with Caretta + Slack
summary: Deal news travels too slowly. How the Caretta + Slack integration pushes call summaries, answers, and deal signals into channels your team already reads.
body_markdown:
The deal visibility gap is the lag between something important happening on a sales call and the people who need to know finding out. The Caretta + Slack integration closes it by pushing call summaries, answers, and deal signals into the channels your team already reads all day.


## 01


What is the deal visibility gap?


Sales calls produce information other people need immediately. A buyer names a blocker the product team should hear. A champion goes quiet in a way the manager should know about. An SE's answer from last week gets contradicted. A competitor shows up in a deal marketing thought was safe.


In most teams, that information travels by hallway physics: it reaches whoever the rep happens to talk to, whenever they happen to talk. The CRM technically holds some of it, but nobody reads CRM records for news. Managers find out about at-risk deals in the weekly pipeline review, which is the most expensive possible place to find out.


The gap is not a lack of data. Calls are recorded, notes exist, dashboards exist. The gap is that none of it arrives where people actually look.


## 02


Why Slack is the right delivery surface


For most B2B teams, Slack is the one surface everyone checks between meetings: sales, product, marketing, and leadership alike. Anything posted to the right channel gets read within hours without anyone changing their habits.


That makes it the natural end of the pipeline for call intelligence. Asking a product manager to browse call recordings for customer feedback fails; posting the three relevant quotes into their channel works. The information has to commute to the reader.


## 03


How does the Caretta + Slack integration work?


Caretta is a real-time AI copilot for sales calls: it joins meetings, helps reps live, and turns each conversation into structured notes and next steps. The Slack integration is how that output reaches the rest of the company:


1. **Call summaries land in Slack.** After a call, Caretta can post the summary and next steps to a deal channel or team channel. The rep approves what gets shared; nothing posts silently.
2. **Ask Caretta questions in Slack.** Caretta holds your organisational knowledge: docs, CRM, and every past call. Anyone can ask it things like "what did Acme say about pricing last week?" or "which open deals mentioned the new API?" and get an answer in the thread, without booking time with the rep.
3. **Signals reach the right people.** Product hears feature requests in the buyer's own words. Managers hear about stalled next steps while the deal can still be saved. The knowledge from calls stops belonging to whoever attended them.


## 04


What changes in practice


Information Without the integration With Caretta + Slack


Call outcome Manager asks the rep, eventually Summary in the deal channel within minutes


Customer feedback Dies in the rep's notes Posted where product reads it


"What did the customer say about X?" Interrupt the rep and wait Ask Caretta in Slack


Deal risk signals Surface at the weekly review Surface the day they happen


The third row compounds quietly. Every "quick question" a rep answers about their own calls is an interruption for them and a delay for the asker. Moving those lookups to Slack gives both sides the time back, and it is the same failure we priced out for buyers in[the real cost of "let me get back to you"](https://www.caretta.so/blog/cost-of-let-me-get-back-to-you) : answers that arrive late lose most of their value.


## 05


Where should the line sit between Slack and your CRM?


Slack is a delivery channel, not a system of record. The structured truth about deals lives in the CRM, where Caretta also writes rep-approved updates. Slack gets the news feed: what happened, what needs attention, what someone asked.


Keep that line firm when you configure the integration. Post summaries to channels people already read; do not create a firehose channel that everyone mutes by week two. A good default is one channel per team or per major deal, plus wherever product collects customer feedback. If a post would not change what its readers do, it should not be posted.


There is a failure mode to avoid: visibility tooling that reps experience as surveillance. The design guards against it in two ways. Reps approve what gets shared, so a rough call does not get broadcast without their say. And the summaries are about deals, not about rep performance; talk-ratio scoring and coaching analytics are a different category of tool and belong in a different, more private workflow. Teams that respect that distinction get reps who share willingly, which is the whole game.


## 06


How to roll it out


1. Connect Slack from Caretta's[integrations](https://www.caretta.so/integrations) page.
2. Start with one team channel receiving call summaries, with rep approval on.
3. Add the ask-Caretta workflow once people have seen a few summaries and trust the source.
4. Invite product and customer-facing teams last, once the sales side runs smoothly. Cross-functional visibility is the payoff, but earn trust inside sales first.


Reps on hard calls also get faster answers to technical questions in the first place; that side of the story is in[answering security and pricing questions on sales calls](https://www.caretta.so/blog/technical-questions-sales-calls) . The Slack integration is what happens to all that knowledge afterwards: it stops being trapped in calls and starts moving at the speed of the company.
